why: The default matters more than the thresholds. If missing QC meant 'proceed', every instrument the pipeline has not reached yet would silently be grade A.

Bars get revised. A confirmatory run that read 'whatever the table says now' cannot be reproduced, and the specific danger is directional: a later revision usually improves the past, so re-reading unpinned silently upgrades a result nobody re-ran.

Not a future bar - a future *edit* to a past bar. Reading at an as-of before the window closed means part of the window was unreadable at that instant; reading at one long after means the run used corrections it could not have had.

The clean twin for the rule above. Demanding a pinned snapshot for every exploratory glance would make the honest path the expensive one, and the agent would stop exploring rather than stop being sloppy.

A model retrained on more data and then scored over a window that now includes some of its own training rows. The score is part in-sample, and because the overlap is usually a few weeks at the boundary, it looks like a mild improvement rather than a bug.

A skill is a procedure. One containing `if sharpe > 1.37` has stopped being a procedure and become a result - fitted somewhere, by someone, on data nobody is citing (ADR-0028). It then applies that number to every future project silently.

The false-rejection half. Annualising by 252, converting to percent, an epsilon guard - a lint that rejected those would make honest skills unwritable, and the agent would stop registering skills rather than stop tuning them.

A model that is told the result was cut asks for a summary; a model that is not, reasons over half a table and reports a number as though it saw all of it. This pair reads the other way round: the oversized payload must be detectable as truncated, and the small one must pass through untouched.
